A1.justification: Despite the changed title and format, both PDFs describe the same MASH research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA and abstention experiments, warm-start ablations, oracle-helper experiments, and out-of-distribution evaluations in its main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results for additional models, abstention baselines, instruction following, mathematical problem solving, and finer-grained analyses.

M1.justification: The constrained warm-start data generation, SFT initialization, GRPO objective, three search penalties, and search-triggered abstention procedure remain unchanged. The algorithms are relocated and renumbered; the additional model experiments apply the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds IFEval instruction following and MATH-Hard mathematical problem solving as general-capability evaluations in Appendix F.3. These substantially broaden task coverage beyond the retained Natural Questions, HotPotQA, 2Wiki, and TriviaQA evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 adds a direct GRPO-trained Ternary abstention baseline to the three-dataset comparison in Table 3 and zero-shot and five-shot Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct comparators in Table 13. These expand the comparison beyond the original search, AFH, DPO, and base-model prompting baselines.

E3.justification: New HotPotQA experiments use Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3-4B with 300 training steps, while the original 3B experiments retain 400 steps. Added protocols include intermediate answerability-bin evaluation, instruct-model prompting, and LM Evaluation Harness tests using 250 samples per available subset and four-shot MATH-Hard prompting.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of dataset answerability distributions, abstention across intermediate accuracy bins, Ternary training collapse, robustness across model scales and families, and retention of general capabilities. These appear in Table 7, Tables 8–14, and Figure 6. The original warm-start, oracle-helper, and out-of-distribution analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report main evaluation averages over four sampled outputs and estimate question answerability using ten responses. Neither adds training-seed variability, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests; the additional result tables do not establish changed uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for the new comparisons and analyses. For example, Table 8 reports Qwen2.5-7B HotPotQA accuracy of 55.13 for MASH versus 51.52 for OTC; Table 14 reports MASH/base scores of 25.20/23.60 on IFEval and 22.80/15.12 on MATH-Hard. Existing results are largely retained, with Search-R1's 2Wiki tool-call average corrected from 3.00 to 2.98 in Table 1.

T1.justification: New Appendix A introduces assumptions, search-conditioned optimal-reward definitions, two lemmas, and a theorem with proofs relating parametric accuracy to help-seeking rewards. v1 contains no corresponding analysis. The addition has an internal inconsistency: the theorem states a greater-than-or-equal condition, whereas Lemma 1 and the proof require strict inequality.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contribution: selective help-seeking training produces efficient search and off-the-shelf abstention without precomputing knowledge boundaries. The multi-hop accuracy and competitive abstention claims remain substantively unchanged; the new experiments primarily supply additional support.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications about MASH and Ternary using exact-match rewards while DPO uses an LLM judge, including resource limits preventing a stronger Ternary evaluation. It also interprets intermediate abstention behavior and general-capability retention. Existing explanations concerning warm-start exploration, retrieval noise, and conservative generalization remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents the Ternary baseline's abstention-detection substring list, settings for the additional model experiments, instruct-prompt reuse, and the harness, sampling, and prompting details for general-task evaluations. The original implementation details, hardware disclosure, and code/checkpoint access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including Wei et al.'s TruthRL, Lin et al. and Gekhman et al. for the theoretical assumptions, and references supporting the new benchmarks and evaluation harness. The established related-work discussion and positioning relative to OTC, Search-R1, and specialized abstention methods remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled, the abstract and warm-start explanation are edited, the former Analysis section is incorporated into Results, and the appendices are reorganized. Most existing prose and the overall argument sequence are retained, so the presentation changes do not constitute wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive changes to table and caption placement. Table 5 is rearranged into stacked dataset blocks; new Tables 7–14 and the Ternary convergence plot are added. Existing warm-start pseudocode and the oracle-helper plot move to the appendices.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the empirical case beyond v1's single-model study through additional model evaluations, direct-RL and instruct-model comparisons, and checks for general-capability degradation. These provide useful support for the unchanged method. The gain is qualified by the exact-match-only Ternary comparison and the new theorem's inconsistent treatment of equal rewards, which prevents accepting its formal guarantee as written.
